thread:
eng-max: incident bot paged SREs for repeated container restarts on gpu-pool-12; observed OOMs during prefill for requests with long context windows. Root: container restarts + node flapping. (Investigating)

oncall-bot: INCIDENT CREATED • Sev=high • paged: @sre-liz, @ops-yuki • symptom: gpu OOMs during prefill -> container RestartCount>5 on gpu-node-12-*. Links: https://ops.redwood/incident/7420005432

sre-liz: acked. pulling logs from the node now. can someone paste the recent nvidia-smi and pod logs? I want driver vs OOM signal.

eng-max: past hour we've seen a spike in requests with >100k tokens in a single prefill (customer A). They bypassed client-side truncation. Prefill tries to materialize KV cache -> OOM.

ops-yuki: nvidia-smi from gpu-node-12-3:
```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 530.41.03    Driver Version: 530.41.03    CUDA Version: 12.1 |
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| 0   A100-SXM4-40GB   Off        00000000:00:1E.0 Off |                    0 |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Processes:                                                                  |
|  No.   PID   Type   Process name                  GPU Mem Usage |
|  2345  1001  C      runtime-server                  39.2GiB |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

infra-dave: pod logs show repeated lines: "prefill: allocating 45.6GiB KV cache for seq_len=65536" followed by "CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY" and kernel panic, container kubelet restarting container.

eng-max: stack trace snippet:
```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory while allocating tensor
  File "/srv/runtime/infer.py", line 412, in prefill
    kv = allocate_kv_cache(tokens_len)
```

sre-liz: judgement call: we need an immediate hot-mitigation. Options: 1) throttle prefill max_context on the gateway (reject/trim incoming requests > X). 2) scale the GPU pool (spin up more nodes) - but that won't stop the ones already allocating. 3) apply node taint/drain to stop noisy neighbors. 4) enable fallback to coldmodel/CPU for long-prefill requests.

support-janet: Customer A is experiencing 5xx errors; they reported session X-291. On our dashboard errors from the service are at 2.4% for the last 10m (baseline 0.02%). Notified CS.

product-oliver: prioritize customer A impact. If we have to throttle, prefer returning 4xx with guidance rather than dropping sessions silently.

ops-yuki: quick mitigation implemented: gateway rule applied to reject prefill requests with context > 32k tokens with 400 + message. RuleID=gw-hotfix-7420. Rolling out now — will report back.

oncall-bot: ACTION_LOG • gw-hotfix-7420 applied to region-us-east-1 by ops-yuki at 7420005480

eng-max: applying a runtime guard as well: hotpatch pushed to reduce max_prefill_batch_size and add allocation cap in the inference process. Patch is in staging and I'll roll to node pool with canary 10%.

infra-dave: draining gpu-node-12-3 to stop restarts and move workloads: `kubectl drain gpu-node-12-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` (rolling). Starting cordon now.

sre-liz: good. after cordon we should evict affected pods and redeploy to fresh nodes with no restart count > 3. Also set autoscaler to prefer larger instance types for this pool (more memory per GPU) — infra, can you create a vm resize ticket?

infra-dave: ticket created: #INF-3291 — increase instance type to a100-80gb for overflow pools. ETA: 45m.

ops-yuki: monitoring: container restarts dropping after drain. Node flapping stopped on that host.

eng-max: telemetry: KV cache allocations per-request now capped. Old pattern: prefill would allocate all tokens at once. New hotpatch streams KV allocation and GC's partial caches for very large sequences. Canary showing 0 OOMs so far in 10m window.

sre-liz: please collect heap profiles and coredumps before we fully delete the old pods. Use `kubectl debug` -> `gcore` to capture if possible.

eng-max: grabbed a core from a crashed container; attaching logs to incident. Saved to s3://redwood-incident-7420005432/cores/

support-janet: Customer A notified: "We're seeing 5xxs and timeouts for long context uploads; a mitigation has been applied to limit max context to 32k tokens. Engineering is working on a safer flow to handle larger contexts." They asked for ETA; provided 2-4 hours for stable remediation.

product-oliver: also add message to status page: short window of degraded service for long-context requests in us-east-1. Please coordinate with comms.

oncall-bot: HANDOFF pending • current oncall: @sre-liz -> next oncall: @ops-yuki at 7420005580

sre-liz: I'll start the postmortem checklist: collect traces, metrics, affected customer list, code lines. Put a temporary guard in the runtime config to fail fast for sequences > 65k until the coldmodel fallback is fully tested.

eng-max: followup plan: implement streaming prefill + incremental KV allocation by chunk; add server-side truncation policy opt-in per-customer; implement a background coldmodel fallback that spills to CPU/GPU-memory-backed shelved weights when allocations exceed threshold.

infra-dave: next steps executed: node drained, gateway rate-limit in place, hotpatch canary at 10% (no OOMs), autoscaler ticket filed.

sre-liz: current status: incident reduced to INVESTIGATING->DEGRADED -> oncall handoff complete. Will remain in this thread. Next update in 30m or earlier on any regression.

ops-yuki: noted. I'm taking follow-up for cleanup and rollout to all nodes. Will update when autoscaler change is live or if we need further mitigation.

support-janet: cc: CS lead. Logging this incident summary into the customer ticket and adding the temporary workaround notes.

eng-max: one more note: add a runtime guard to log the originating request ID + token count for any prefill > 16k for 24h so we can understand prevalence.

product-oliver: approved. include a short FAQ for customers about how to avoid long-prefill OOMs and recommended client-side truncation.

sre-liz: closing update for now: mitigation active, customer notified, handoff done. Will open an RCA doc and assign owners for long-term fixes. :thumbsup:
summary: GPU OOM during prefill triggered container restarts on gpu-node-12-3. Immediate mitigations: gateway limit on context size, runtime hotpatch to cap allocations, drain affected node. Customer impacted (5xxs) for long-context uploads; mitigation communicated. Follow-ups: streaming prefill, coldmodel fallback, autoscaler instance resize ticket.#INF-3291
